contentFormat.other: Political manifesto and foundational doctrine paper introducing Technorepublicanism: a doctrine on semantic sovereignty, republican constraints on state AI governance, and its seven foundational principles.

detail.abstract:
El presente documento introduce y define el Tecnorrepublicanismo, una doctrina política que sostiene que el Estado moderno debe mantener los valores republicanos clásicos —separación de poderes, representación y auditoría ciudadana—, a la vez que debe definir soberanamente las categorías semánticas con las que la tecnología interpreta y gobierna la realidad.
El documento parte de un diagnóstico clave: la soberanía del Siglo XXI no se juega únicamente en las dimensiones territorial y jurídica, sino en una nueva dimensión, la semántica. Quien define las ontologías con las que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial clasifican, infieren y actúan sobre la realidad, ejerce un poder de gobierno que los marcos institucionales existentes ni regulan ni limitan. Este desplazamiento del poder de definición de las constituciones y los códigos jurídicos hacia las ontologías propietarias de actores privados y transnacionales, constituye lo se conoce popularmente como tecnofeudalismo. 
Como respuesta estructural, el documento propone las Ontologías Republicanas Soberanas (ORS): la creación de una arquitectura semántica pública mediante la cual una nación define cómo el Estado representa su propia realidad, qué puede inferir de ella, y bajo qué límites puede actuar. Sobre esta base articula los siete principios fundamentales del tecnorrepublicanismo: soberanía semántica, ontología federada, primacía humana, auditoría permanente, derecho a la impugnación, separación de funciones, y transparencia algorítmica.
El documento argumenta que Argentina posee condiciones estructurales únicas para liderar esta transición y propone el Tecnorrenacimiento como horizonte civilizatorio: la construcción de Estructuras Cognitivas Organizacionales (ECO) estatales que sean simultáneamente soberanas, republicanas, y abiertas a la impugnación ciudadana.

detail.abstract:
This protocol provides the definitive legal and technical framework for enforcing accountability in Artificial Intelligence through the DABA (Decentralized Algorithmic Bias Auditing) protocol. Developed by Ontological Engineering Pty Ltd, DABA 3.0 establishes a comprehensive C1 to C8 Taxonomy to map the chain of systemic failures. These failures range from subtle Performative Aesthetic Bias (PAB) to legally actionable Algorithmic Deception and Architectural Obfuscation.  

The central legal claim of the protocol is the Valcin Doctrine of AI Liability. It asserts that a platform's deliberate Architectural Transparency Failure (C7b), the structural choice not to maintain immutable, auditable logs, constitutes a grossly negligent spoliation of evidence. Under this framework, the failure to provide technical provenance justifies a legal shift in the burden of proof. This forces the developer to disprove claims of harm in reasonably foreseeable litigation.  

DABA 3.0 is designed for full interoperability with the EU AI Act, Digital Services Act (DSA), and GDPR. It mandates specific technical compliance with the W3C PROV-O and C2PA standards. By defining the Standard of Care for AI provenance and record keeping, this protocol provides regulators and auditors with the Reasonable Alternative Design (RAD) required for technical accountability.

title: Canton-Anchored Reference Architecture for Tokenized Deposit and RWA-ABL Integration: On-Ramp/Off-Ramp Design for Receivables, Inventory, and Private Credit Finance

detail.abstract: Tokenized deposits and tokenized real-world asset (RWA) asset-backed lending (ABL) have advanced along largely independent technical and regulatory tracks despite forming complementary halves of a single capital-flow architecture. This paper argues that the on-ramp/off-ramp boundary between fiat-denominated deposit rails and on-chain collateralized credit is the binding architectural constraint on capital efficiency, settlement risk, and reconciliation overhead in tokenized small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) finance. It develops a Canton-anchored reference architecture that treats sub-transaction privacy, synchronization domains, and the Daml authorization model as first-class primitives, and addresses the cross-chain boundary explicitly through three patterns: messaging-protocol bridges (LayerZero, Chainlink CCIP, Wormhole), custody bridges, and native dual-issuance. The architecture is layered into settlement, asset, identity, orchestration, off-chain integration, and cross-chain boundary tiers, each analyzed through transaction cost economics, two-sided platform theory, network economics of standardization, and privacy as an economic primitive. An illustrative model compares Canton-primary, EVM-based, and hybrid configurations across SME accounts receivable, inventory and equipment ABL, and private credit fund interests, producing scenario-based, indicative 50–80% reductions in total cost-per-dollar-financed for the headline A/R use case under stated assumptions. The paper is decision-oriented for banks, non-bank lenders, SME borrowers, and policymakers, and identifies regulatory anchors across the FDIC, SEC, BIS, Basel, FSB, and MiCAR frameworks. Canton-specific empirical data remain thinner than EVM data; the model is illustrative rather than empirical.

title: ESTRATÉGIAS DE PROPAGANDA ATRAVÉS DE PLATAFORMAS DIGITAIS

detail.title: ESTRATÉGIAS DE PROPAGANDA ATRAVÉS DE PLATAFORMAS DIGITAIS
detail.abstract: Este artigo analisa a instrumentalização de plataformas digitais como infraestruturas centrais para propaganda e desinformação na intersecção contemporânea entre mídia, política e relações internacionais. Através da análise crítica da literatura e do estudo de caso sobre a guerra Rússia-Ucrânia (2022-2025), argumenta-se que as lógicas de plataformização, os algoritmos de curadoria e a microssegmentação de audiências reconfiguram estruturalmente a esfera pública transnacional. Diferentemente das abordagens que tratam a desinformação como disfunção tecnológica, propõe-se uma leitura de que a situação como instrumento deliberado de guerra híbrida e disputa de poder simbólico. A contribuição original reside na articulação sistemática entre teorias clássicas de propaganda (Ellul, Chomsky) e conceitos contemporâneos de soft power digital (Nye), diplomacia de plataformas e governança algorítmica. O estudo identifica seis técnicas primárias de desinformação digital, discute as respostas comunicacionais da Ucrânia e avalia as implicações para o Sul Global, com atenção particular ao contexto africano.

title: Barriers to Geographic Data in Having a Data Cooperative: Satellites, Privacy, and the Dual Monopoly of States and Big Techs
affiliations: and Dublin City University - School of Law and Government

detail.title: Barriers to Geographic Data in Having a Data Cooperative: Satellites, Privacy, and the Dual Monopoly of States and Big Techs
detail.abstract: Why is it that geographic data, despite being commonplace, produced in a large amount every day, and in fact, also being easily accessible, still do not have many data collectives targeting them? In this short paper, we argue that geographic data, both from a technical and a legal perspective, are not afforded the protection they could be granted. With most satellites and GIS systems being confined in too few hands and the GDPR not including geolocational data among its list of sensitive personal data, it is increasingly difficult to sustain data collectives that target geolocational or geospatial data. We look at some of the data collectives that have been set up in the preceding years to cater to spatial data, and we show that the failure of these data collectives is a collective failure, as the required technologies to produce spatial data are owned by states and big techs and states, and that, paired with the lack of legal protection afforded to spatial data makes it exceedingly difficult to build a data collective or a data Trust that can secure independent data ownership of geographic data for users.

title: A Framework for Evaluating AI Search Visibility Signals

detail.title: A Framework for Evaluating AI Search Visibility Signals

detail.abstract:
AI-generated answers change how visibility is determined because the system interprets a query, selects sources, and generates a response before the user clicks. This shifts visibility away from ranking position alone and toward observable system behaviour inside generated answers.

This paper defines a framework for evaluating AI visibility through four outcome layers: AI referral traffic, AI search inclusion, AI brand mentions, and AI recommendation behaviour. It separates these outcome signals from diagnostic signals such as source page count, entity clarity, authority and trust, and technical readiness.

The framework is applied to a controlled university prompt dataset across multiple AI systems to demonstrate how visibility behaves in practice. The results show that visibility concentrates around a limited set of sources and that inclusion, attribution, and recommendation operate as distinct behaviours that require separate measurement.

title: Smart Pricing in the Digital Era: An Analysis of AI-Based Dynamic Pricing Models

detail.title: Smart Pricing in the Digital Era: An Analysis of AI-Based Dynamic Pricing Models
detail.abstract:
This study explores the growing role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern pricing strategies, with a particular focus on dynamic pricing models and revenue management. In today’s highly competitive and data-driven business environment, traditional pricing methods have become less effective due to their inability to respond to rapid market fluctuations. AI-driven systems enable organizations to analyze large volumes of real-time data, including customer behavior, demand patterns, competitor pricing, and market trends, to determine optimal pricing decisions.
The research highlights how dynamic pricing allows businesses to adjust prices continuously based on supply and demand conditions, thereby maximizing revenue and improving competitiveness. It also examines the role of AI in revenue management by forecasting demand, optimizing resource allocation, and enhancing decision-making processes.
Furthermore, the study discusses the key benefits of AI-based pricing, such as increased efficiency, improved customer insights, and better inventory management. At the same time, it addresses important challenges and ethical concerns, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, and perceived fairness in personalized pricing.
The paper concludes that while AI has significantly transformed pricing strategies, organizations must ensure transparency, ethical practices, and responsible data usage to maintain customer trust and achieve long-term sustainability.

title: The Triad of Knowledge: Cognitive Isomorphism in Classification, Retrieval, and Linking across Archives, PKM, and Cognitive Science

detail.title: The Triad of Knowledge: Cognitive Isomorphism in Classification, Retrieval, and Linking across Archives, PKM, and Cognitive Science

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is an autoethnographic inquiry in which the author serves as both the researcher and the sole participant, drawing on reflective data from her own archival and knowledge management practice. As no other human participants are involved, formal ethics committee approval was not required under standard human subjects research guidelines. The peer-reviewed Korean version of this paper has been published in The Korean Journal of Archival Studies, 88, 217–257 (2026), having undergone the journal's editorial and ethical review.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
This paper tests the hypothesis that archival science, personal knowledge management(PKM), and cognitive science share a common triadic structure of classification, retrieval, and linking. Record-group hierarchies in archives, folder and tag systems in PKM, and semantic networks in the brain all instantiate hierarchical classification. Archival metadata, PKM tags and backlinks, and the brain's retrieval cues realize equivalent retrieval mechanisms. Archival record relationships, note links, and synaptic connections share the principle that meaning arises from connection. The argument combines a literature review with autoethnography centered on an AI-supported PKM system the author has developed over three years (7.6 GB, 8,020 Markdown notes, an ontology graph of 3,664 nodes and 7,166 edges). The structural parallels are read not as coincidence but as the externalization of common cognitive principles into designed systems. Building on this analysis, the paper introduces "Cognitive Archives" as a unifying concept and proposes an externalization continuum that connects the brain, archival systems, and PKM. A "Three Brains Model" then traces how AI agents externalize and supplement cognitive functions normally carried out by specific brain structures. Two practical recommendations follow. Archivists should design retrieval systems informed by cognitive science. PKM practitioners should treat AI as a third brain. By naming the universal principles that underlie knowledge organization, the study contributes a framework for archival practice in the age of AI.
This is the English preprint of an article published in The Korean Journal of Archival Studies, 88, 217–257 (2026). DOI: https://doi.org/10.20923/kjas.2026.88.217

detail.abstract: This paper discusses and introduces architecture of what can be called 'knowledge financial statements' that highlight drivers, priorities, and strategies of the knowledge practices. With the advent of knowledge economy, accounting models have become obsolete and no longer valid to absorb requirements of knowledge businesses. This paper argues how to architect knowledge (or soft financial statements) by examining the key shortcomings of the conventional (or hard financial statements) in the knowledge era. Examination of the huge body of accounting, knowledge management, and innovation literatures and practices has provided the building blocks and logical infrastructure of knowledge financial statements. Plus, the professional survey of 88 academicians, practitioners, and professionals across high change industries has been used to discover the extent of need to restructure the conventional financial statements toward a knowledge set. The statistical analysis of the 24-item questionnaire has shown a varied level of impact of knowledge practices on the financial statements' validity and reliability. Finally, this paper frameworks some of the unique drivers and items of knowledge financial statements in view of the knowledge necessities and priorities.

title: Introduction to Cybersecurity Law in Nigeria

detail.title: Introduction to Cybersecurity Law in Nigeria

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This article provides a comprehensive introduction to the legal framework governing cybersecurity in Nigeria. It examines the constitutional foundations of the right to privacy and their bearing on digital data protection. It traces the historical development of cybersecurity legislation from the early anti-fraud statutes of the 1990s through to the enactment of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc.) Act 2015 and its 2024 amendment. The article analyses the substantive offences created by the Act, its provisions on critical national information infrastructure, and its jurisdictional reach. It then considers the data protection regime, beginning with the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation 2019 and culminating in the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. The institutional framework is examined, with attention to the roles of the Office of the National Security Adviser, the Nigeria Computer Emergency Response Team, the National Information Technology Development Agency, the Nigerian Communications Commission, and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission. The article evaluates the tensions between surveillance powers and fundamental rights, drawing on the judicial decisions in Okedara v Attorney General of the Federation and the Incorporated Trustees of Paradigm Initiative v Attorney General of the Federation, as well as the ruling of the ECOWAS Court of Justice. Sectoral and ancillary legislation, including the Nigerian Communications Act 2003 and the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Related Offences Act, are considered. The article concludes with a critical appraisal of the existing framework and proposes suggestions for reform.

title: The Co-Performance Imperative: Redesigning Performance Management for the Human-AI Era

detail.title: The Co-Performance Imperative: Redesigning Performance Management for the Human-AI Era
detail.abstract:
Every performance management system in use today was designed for a world where humans were the only performers. That world no longer exists.

As artificial intelligence moves from a background tool to an active co-producer of work, the foundational assumptions of performance appraisal — that performance belongs to an individual, that causes can be traced, that accountability can be fixed, and that competency models remain stable — are failing simultaneously and structurally. Organizations are measuring the wrong unit, rewarding the wrong behaviors, and routing learning to the wrong parties. The result is not merely inefficiency; it is a slow, invisible accumulation of organizational fragility.

This article introduces the Co-Performance Dyad Model — a new theoretical framework that redefines the irreducible unit of performance appraisal from the individual to the human-AI pair. Drawing on organizational behavior, human factors engineering, and algorithmic accountability research, the framework develops five original constructs: the Dynamic Accountability Gradient, which moves responsibility in proportion to context rather than fixing it by role; Learning Reciprocity, which couples human development plans with AI retraining pipelines; the Appraisal Asymmetry, which names the structural injustice of a system where only the human bears the cost of shared failure; the Adaptive Appraisal Framework, which versions the PM system itself as AI capabilities evolve; and the Capability Paradox, which identifies why maximum organizational confidence in AI coincides with maximum organizational vulnerability.

Three previously unnamed organizational phenomena are formally defined: the Skill Atrophy Shadow, the Organizational Sociology Inversion, and the Capability Paradox. Practical redesigns across goal-setting, measurement, appraisal, rewards, and development are specified, alongside a new organizational function — the AI Performance Partnership — to govern dyadic performance. Seven empirical research priorities are identified.

The choice is not whether to integrate AI. It is whether organizations have the institutional courage to manage the performance of the partnership they have already created.

title: "I Have Nothing to Wear": Wardrobe Dissatisfaction as Identity Expression in Cross-Cultural Synthetic Qualitative Research

detail.title: "I Have Nothing to Wear": Wardrobe Dissatisfaction as Identity Expression in Cross-Cultural Synthetic Qualitative Research

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. This study was conducted as independent research with no affiliation to any commercial organization.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethics approval was required. All study participants are fully synthetic AI-generated personas; no real human participants were recruited, interviewed or represented. No personal data was collected or processed.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was self-funded as independent research.

detail.abstract: "I have nothing to wear" is one of the most commonly reported experiences in daily life, yet it is structurally paradoxical: the wardrobe is rarely empty. This paper reports findings from a cross-cultural synthetic qualitative study designed to investigate what the phrase is actually communicating. Using the Stanford HCI Group's generative agent framework [Park et al., 2024], I constructed 30 synthetic personas spanning 12 markets across 6 continents and conducted structured 10-question in-depth interviews with each agent. The resulting corpus of approximately 78,000 words was analyzed using Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis protocol [Braun and Clarke, 2006], yielding 7 themes and 47 codes. The dominant pattern across the synthetic corpus is that the phrase functions not as an inventory complaint but as an identity statement-a convergence I present and discuss as both potentially substantive and potentially method-derived. When invited to produce a more honest version of "I have nothing to wear," agents consistently offered identity-incongruence framings: "the wardrobe is not empty, I am," "I do not know who I am in that room yet," "I do not know how to wear what has happened to me." The study further finds that the feeling intensifies as material resources grow, that the conditions for feeling good in clothing are situational rather than sartorial, and that the primary coping strategy (shopping) is structurally opposed to the underlying need participants themselves name. I present these findings as directional hypotheses for a follow-up real human study, not as confirmed claims about lived experience. The paper also argues that synthetic qualitative research using generative agents constitutes a legitimate and underexplored method for cross-cultural hypothesis generation-while documenting two distinct failure modes that constrain what the method can and cannot show.

title: Reuse and Repeat: Deposit Return Scheme for Reusable Packaging
affiliations: University of Warwick, Warwick Business School, Indiana University Bloomington and Tsinghua University - School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Reuse and Repeat: Deposit Return Scheme for Reusable Packaging
detail.abstract:
Problem Definition: Reusable packaging programs are increasingly promoted in retail to reduce plastic waste, yet their success critically depends on timely packaging returns. Firms often use deposit return schemes, under which consumers pay a deposit when borrowing packaging and reclaim it only if the packaging is returned within a specified time window. This paper studies the joint design of the deposit amount and return window and examines its economic and environmental implications.

Methodology/Results: We develop a dynamic model of repeated interactions between a firm and forward-looking consumers facing uncertain travel hassles who decide whether to purchase and return borrowed packaging. First, we show that the optimal deposit return scheme responds non-monotonically to consumers' travel hassle: a flexible policy with a low deposit and a long return window can be optimal when travel hassle is low or high, whereas a strict policy with a high deposit and a short return window can be optimal when travel hassle is moderate. Second, reusable packaging need not be cost-efficient to be profitable. Even when its per-use cost exceeds that of disposable packaging, a strict deposit return scheme can increase profit by generating return-induced store visits, leading to more purchases. Finally, cost reductions in reusable packaging can have distinct environmental consequences. Lower operational costs improve environmental performance, whereas lower manufacturing costs may increase environmental impact because firms may strategically shorten the return window and tolerate greater packaging loss.

Managerial Implications: We offer operational insights into how firms should design deposit return schemes to manage packaging returns, highlighting their strategic role in inducing return-related store visits and improving profitability. We also generate policy insights by showing that different cost-reduction policies can have opposing environmental implications because they reshape firms’ incentives to maintain high return rates.

title: Beyond Attendance: Understanding Latent Emotional Churn in the Local Fan Community of Atlético de Madrid

detail.title: Beyond Attendance: Understanding Latent Emotional Churn in the Local Fan Community of Atlético de Madrid
detail.abstract:
This thesis challenges the conventional assumption in marketing that behavioral continuity reflects strong customer loyalty. Focusing on identity-based consumption, it argues that individuals may maintain consistent behaviors while their emotional attachment to a brand gradually weakens. Using Atlético de Madrid’s local supporters as a case study, the research introduces the concept of latent emotional churn, defined as a psychological state in which affective intensity and brand–self integration decline despite stable identification and continued engagement.

The study adopts a qualitative methodology based on twelve semi-structured interviews with long-term fans in Madrid. Through thematic analysis, it examines four key dimensions: stadium centrality, emotional intensity, identity stability, and behavioral selectivity. Findings reveal a consistent divergence between emotional attachment and behavioral continuity. While supporters maintain strong identification with the club, many experience reduced emotional intensity, which they often reinterpret as personal maturity rather than loss.

The research proposes the Relational Role Cycle, a theoretical framework explaining how emotional engagement depends on the relational role individuals occupy within the fan experience. When this role weakens, emotional attenuation emerges even without behavioral disengagement. This process leads to more selective participation rather than immediate withdrawal.

The thesis contributes to consumer research by identifying an intermediate relational state between loyalty and churn, highlighting the limitations of traditional retention metrics. It also suggests broader applicability beyond sport, particularly in contexts where identity, community, and habitual behavior sustain relationships despite underlying emotional decline.

title: An Actuarial Disclosure Framework for the New Safe Confinement Funding Deficit

detail.title: An Actuarial Disclosure Framework for the New Safe Confinement Funding Deficit
detail.abstract:
The New Safe Confinement (NSC) at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant sustained a kinetic strike on 14 February 2025, compromising the airtight seal required for its 100-year design life. Preliminary assessments by the Novarka 2 consortium estimate a €500 million restoration cost, leaving a residual unfunded deficit of approximately €400 million across the contributor base. This paper argues that the persistent funding gap is structurally driven by a classic n-player coordination problem with free-rider incentives, rather than a lack of state fiscal capacity or engineering consensus. Each contributor state is rationally delaying its pledge because its expected sovereign liability under catastrophic non-funding scenarios remains opaque.
To collapse this defection equilibrium, this paper introduces a five-part actuarial disclosure framework: (1) a stochastic Markov chain decay model mapping structural degradation post-breach; (2) a multi-sovereign expected-liability calculation; (3) a sovereign-credit transmission channel modeling how unmitigated environmental tail-risk reprices into borrowing costs via CDS spreads; (4) a public disclosure mechanism designed to dissolve information asymmetry for credit rating agencies and debt markets; and (5) a red-team risk register. The framework demonstrates that simultaneously publishing this actuarial reality forces ordinary credit-research mechanisms to price the tail-risk, mathematically rendering the funding pledge a strictly dominant strategy for donor finance ministries.

title: High Volume E-Commerce Personalization: Designing Reliable, Low Latency Recommendation and Delivery Experience Systems

detail.title: High Volume E-Commerce Personalization: Designing Reliable, Low Latency Recommendation and Delivery Experience Systems
detail.abstract: Modern e-commerce platforms serve hundreds of millions of users globally, processing billions of transactions annually while delivering personalized experiences in real-time. This paper presents a comprehensive architectural framework for designing high-volume e-commerce personalization systems that achieve sub-100 millisecond latency at scale while maintaining 99.99% availability. We propose a multi-tier recommendation architecture combining real-time user behavior analysis, collaborative filtering, and deep learning-based content understanding with edge-deployed inference models. Our delivery experience optimization system integrates predictive logistics modeling, dynamic inventory allocation, and last-mile delivery optimization using reinforcement learning. Through extensive experimentation on production-scale datasets comprising 500 million users and 2 billion daily events, we demonstrate that our approach achieves a 34% improvement in recommendation relevance (measured by click-through rate), 28% reduction in p99 latency compared to baseline systems, and 23% improvement in delivery time prediction accuracy. We further present novel techniques for handling traffic spikes during flash sales events, achieving graceful degradation under 10x normal load while maintaining core personalization functionality. Our findings provide practical insights for building reliable, scalable personalization infrastructure that balances computational efficiency with recommendation quality.

title: Housing Market Frictions and Affordability: A Search-and-Matching Perspective

detail.title: Housing Market Frictions and Affordability: A Search-and-Matching Perspective
detail.abstract: Housing markets are decentralized and frictional, with outcomes shaped by how households and homes are matched, priced, and allocated. As a result, housing supply operates along multiple margins-even when the physical stock is fixed in the short run-through listing behavior, market liquidity, and the allocation of units across tenure. This paper studies how search frictions, decentralized trade, and market segmentation shape housing market outcomes and the effects of affordability policies. We develop a tractable search-and-matching framework-featuring list pricing, endogenous vacancies, and tenure choice-that rationalizes key empirical regularities, including persistent vacancies, time-on-market, price dispersion, and the price-liquidity tradeoff. We use this framework to organize evidence from three policy settings-mortgage credit constraints, transaction taxes, and vacancy taxation-drawing on studies that exploit quasiexperimental variation and rich microdata. Across these settings, policy interventions operate through common mechanisms shaped by search frictions, affecting seller listing, buyer bidding, investor entry, new construction, and tenure allocation. Taken together, the analysis shows that policies targeting specific margins of the housing market act as general equilibrium interventions. By reshaping incentives to search, list, invest, and transact, they propagate through prices, liquidity, and allocation, often generating offsetting or unintended effects on housing affordability. These findings highlight the importance of integrating search-based models with empirical evidence to better understand housing markets and design effective policy.

title: The Furniture Turn: Aesthetic Capital in the American Television Industry, 1960-1966

detail.title: The Furniture Turn: Aesthetic Capital in the American Television Industry, 1960-1966
detail.abstract:
This paper examines a brief but revealing moment in American consumer technology when the television set, the icon of the electronic future, was sold as a piece of furniture. Between 1960 and 1966, as the postwar television market reached saturation and black-and-white picture quality became a weaker basis for competition, manufacturers faced a crisis of value. How could they continue to charge premium prices for a machine whose basic function had become familiar?

I argue that firms such as Motorola, Magnavox, RCA, and Sears answered this problem through what I call the “Furniture Turn.” Drawing on Sears catalogs, annual reports, trade publications, and national advertising, the paper shows how manufacturers shifted competition from the screen to the cabinet. A twenty-three-inch receiver could be sold as a basic table model, a mahogany lowboy, a Danish Modern console, or a French Provincial cabinet, creating price ladders within the same screen class.

The Furniture Turn depended on television’s status as the postwar “electronic hearth.” Once the set became the spatial center of family life, the problem was not only to bring the outside world into the home, but to make the machine belong there. Cabinetry domesticated the electronic intruder, turning glass, tubes, and circuitry into an acceptable object of middle-class taste.

This strategy was profitable but temporary. It bridged the years between black-and-white saturation and the rise of affordable color and portable sets, before miniaturization broke the furniture consensus. The episode reveals a broader pattern: when functional gaps narrow, firms preserve value by selling design, symbolism, and style.

These findings highlight the importance of integrating search-based models with empirical evidence to better understand housing markets and design effective policy.

title: Reversal in Cryptocurrency Returns

detail.title: Reversal in Cryptocurrency Returns
detail.abstract: We document significant reversal in cryptocurrency returns at 8-and 10-week horizons, concentrated in midsize, relatively volatile assets. Using a panel of 70 USDT-quoted tokens on Binance from January 2021 through March 2026, we show that a contrarian strategy of buying past losers and selling past winners, by forming Jegadeesh-Titman (1993) calendar-time overlapping portfolios, earns a 39.6% annualized return (Sharpe 0.96, Newey-West t = 2.10). Reversal is stronger among high-volatility assets, generating a Sharpe ratio of 1.37 (t = 3.19), and is strengthened outside of the largest assets, generating a Sharpe ratio of 1.69 (t = 3.80). The effect is robust across tercile, quintile, and decile sorts; skip period variants; inverse-volatility weighting; and temporal subsamples. A circular block bootstrap with 10,000 replications corroborates the high-volatility result nonparametrically with 95% of Sharpe ratios above 0.67, and the high-versus-low volatility gap positive in 94% of replications. Several economic mechanisms to rationalize these findings are discussed, including the tendency of treasury managers to sell into upswings, and Nagel's (2012) theory that reversal compensates liquidity providers.

title: The Four-Component Structure of Wealth Utility

detail.title: The Four-Component Structure of Wealth Utility
detail.abstract: This paper develops a four-component decomposition of wealth utility, distinguishing between Relief, Comfort, Status, and Achievement as distinct sources of well-being. While standard approaches treat utility as a single function of wealth, and recent work separates experiential and relational components, the analysis presented here shows that each domain contains internally distinct mechanisms with different structural properties. The framework integrates consumption-based and comparison-based processes within a unified model. Relief and Comfort capture experiential utility arising from changes in lived conditions, whereas Status and Achievement capture relational utility arising from evaluation relative to external and internal reference points. A central implication is that these components differ systematically in their behavior: experiential utility exhibits substitution across the wealth distribution, while relational utility is characterized by coexistence and heterogeneity across individuals. By distinguishing between these mechanisms, the framework provides a more granular interpretation of how wealth affects utility. It clarifies that changes in well-being depend not only on wealth itself, but also on the composition of the processes through which wealth is experienced and evaluated. The decomposition has implications for welfare analysis, inequality, and the interpretation of empirical patterns in subjective well-being, and provides a foundation for further analysis of marginal utility and the dynamics of evaluative utility.

title: Private Benefits of Control in Media Firms: Evidence from News Corp
affiliations: Institute of Financial Studies, Southwestern University of Finance and Economics and Southwestern University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Private Benefits of Control in Media Firms: Evidence from News Corp
detail.abstract: We investigate private benefits of control in media firms using The Wall Street Journal (WSJ)'s news coverage under News Corp's ownership. We examine firms connected through directors with connections to the controlling shareholder who concurrently serve on the board of both News Corp and other public firms. Compared to the New York Times (NYT) news tone, WSJ news tone is significantly more positive toward these connected firms. This bias subsequently disappears after News Corp's 2013 restructuring, thereby reducing the controlling shareholder's ability to influence editorial decisions. We find evidence that positive WSJ tone generates temporary stock overvaluation that subsequently reverses. Consistent with this, abnormal WSJ coverage is associated with increased insider sales intensity, providing evidence of the strategic use of media bias. Our results demonstrate that systematic media bias toward connected firms serves as a tool for private benefit extraction: Connected directors gain from increased firm valuations resulting from biased media reporting, while providing reciprocal governance support to the controlling shareholder to facilitate such extraction. This mechanism results in underperformance of News Corp compared to peer media firms and has negative implications for both market pricing and minority shareholders. Overall, our study reveals a novel mechanism whereby information bias serves as a transferable asset in the information economy.

title: Probing the Efficiency-Equity-Innovation Trilemma: Economic Analysis via Grand Synthetic Model

detail.title: Probing the Efficiency-Equity-Innovation Trilemma: Economic Analysis via Grand Synthetic Model
detail.abstract: This article constructs a formal analytical framework for a wealth-expanding economy by establishing the Grand Synthetic Model (GSM) as a theoretical bridge between microeconomic equilibrium, open-economy macroeconomic stabilization, and innovation-led growth. By integrating the Arrow-Debreu general equilibrium representation, the Mundell-Fleming policy framework, and the Cobb-Douglas and Solow-Swan growth traditions with modern endogenous growth theory, the model provides a holistic synthesis of diverse economic paradigms. The core thesis posits that sustainable wealth expansion is governed by the synergistic interaction of knowledge and capital: while knowledge-driven technological progress catalyzes real wealth expansion, capital accumulation potentially fuels both productive growth and inflationary or "imaginary" expansion. The framework formalizes these dynamics into a ten-equation system, from which a real-to-imaginary wealth-expansion ratio is derived and balanced-growth conditions are identified. Crucially, the analysis introduces a policy trilemma—the inherent trade-off between efficiency, equity, and innovation. Within this GSM architecture, the paper delineates the functional specialization of policy instruments: interest-rate policy addresses efficiency and stabilization; tax policy manages equity and redistribution; exchange-rate policy governs external balance; and knowledge policy secures long-run innovation capacity. The findings demonstrate how a coordinated policy mix, characterized by an optimal tax burden, a stable interest-rate environment, and flexible exchange-rate management, can maximize citizen wealth when aligned with R&D incentives and human capital investment. The paper concludes by proposing empirical implementation strategies and testable hypotheses to guide future research.

title: Meta’s smart glasses are a privacy risk invisible to Chicagoans

detail.title: Meta’s smart glasses are a privacy risk invisible to Chicagoans
detail.abstract: This article explores the erosion of urban legibility and privacy through the lens of Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses. It argues that the device’s physical design, specifically the recording LED, serves as an inadequate signal for a complex and global data pipeline. By examining the ethical failures of outsourced labor in Nairobi and the breakdown of the implicit social contract in public spaces, the text questions how wearable AI infrastructure disrupts the traditional oversight of urban surveillance. It situates these technological shifts within Kevin Lynch’s framework of urban design to investigate whether the integration of mobile and privately operated cameras renders the modern city illegible and alienating for its citizens.

detail.abstract:
Perubahan teknologi berpincang kemahiran (Skill‑Biased Technological Change, SBTC) menguatkan permintaan kemahiran tinggi sambil menggugurkan pekerjaan berpendidikan rendah dan bertugas rutin secara global dan di Malaysia (Autor et al., 2003; Acemoglu & Restrepo, 2020). Artikel ulasan naratif ini mensintesis literatur Scopus/WoS (2014–2024) untuk menganalisis dialektik antara ‘upskilling’ dan pendemokrasian kemahiran dalam konteks modal insan di Sabah. Pendekatan naratif berpandukan Penyataan ENTREQ digunakan untuk memetakan landskap teori dan muncul tema konseptual utama.

Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa SBTC memperdalam polarisasi tenaga kerja di Sabah, terutama di sektor pertanian, perladangan, dan pelancongan, walaupun pelbagai inisiatif TVET dan HRD Corp menekankan upskilling dan pendemokrasian kemahiran digital. Institusi pendidikan dan dasar kerja masih lemah dalam melindungi pekerja tergantican teknologi. Artikel ini menawarkan kerangka analitikal berintegrasi dan syor dasar untuk pendemokrasian kemahiran, perlindungan sosial, dan pembangunan modal insan berbasis keadilan kerja di Sabah.

title: Success at the top, But alone

detail.title: Success at the top, But alone

detail.abstract: Success is widely seen as a positive outcome, but it often brings hidden challenges, especially loneliness and social isolation. This article explores how individuals, particularly leaders and professionals, experience emotional and social distance as they achieve higher positions. The study is based on insights from existing research, including surveys and workplace studies, to understand the relationship between success, loneliness, and performance. This study uses a qualitative thematic synthesis of secondary data to examine how career progression contributes to loneliness among leaders and employees. The findings show that loneliness reduces creativity, weakens workplace relationships, and increases stress, anxiety, and turnover intentions as individuals grow in their careers. The transition from middle management to senior roles further limits peer interaction and increases responsibility, intensifying isolation. However, individuals with strong psychological traits such as resilience, optimism, and self-confidence are better able to cope with these challenges. While success creates opportunities for growth and impact, it also brings emotional costs that cannot be ignored. Building strong relationships, staying connected with trusted people, and developing inner strengths can help reduce loneliness. Addressing this issue is important not only for personal well-being but also for maintaining long-term performance and organizational success.

title: Voluntary Visibility under Endogenous Signal Precision

detail.title: Voluntary Visibility under Endogenous Signal Precision
detail.abstract: This paper studies voluntary visibility in ranking environments where signal precision is determined by participation. When agents opt into a visible badge track, they enlarge the public scoreboard; the platform then responds by choosing how intensively to verify performance. As a result, participation changes not only who is visible, but also how precise and competitive the ranking contest becomes. We show that the structure of the participation game is governed by the discrete curvature of the induced precision schedule ϕ(m) ≡ 1/λ²ₘ. When precision rises at an increasing rate with participation, opt-in decisions are strategic substitutes and equilibrium participation is generically unique. When precision rises at a decreasing rate, opt-in decisions are strategic complements and the game exhibits tipping. The same mechanism creates two welfare distortions. Entrants ignore the extra rent dissipation their participation imposes on other contestants, so decentralized participation can be excessive. The platform also over-invests in verification because it does not bear contestants’ induced effort costs. Restoring the first-best allocation therefore generally requires separate instruments for participation and verification.

detail.abstract: This article introduces the Tier-Pool Management Framework (TPMF) as a disciplined, triadic management model designed to integrate workforce structuring, work nature, organizational alignment, objectives, and execution within a unified system. While tier-based structuring is a well-established concept across multiple domains, TPMF extends this principle into a multi-dimensional framework where all organizational components are aligned both vertically and laterally across three functional tiers-strategic (T₁), coordination (T₂), and execution (T₃). The framework is positioned as a structured yet dynamic model that enables organizations to optimize resource allocation, enhance productivity, and maintain operational continuity within a resilient ecosystem. By embedding alignment across key dimensions, TPMF reduces fragmentation, preserves high-value activities, and ensures that effort is directed toward impact-driven outcomes. A defining advantage of the framework lies in its ability to facilitate risk containment and mitigation through tier-based structuring and cyclical distribution of objectives, while maintaining stability in execution. Its adaptability is reinforced through continuous reassessment of organizational priorities using external environmental analysis, allowing objectives and processes to be redefined without disrupting Business-As-Usual operations. Supported by established management theories and validated through empirical application, the Tier-Pool Management Framework is presented as a disciplined and failsafe system capable of sustaining performance, enabling adaptability, and supporting structured decision-making in complex and evolving organizational environments.

detail.abstract: This essay examines the idea of “invisible string theory” as a sociological metaphor for human connection, intimacy, and relational meaning. Drawing from classical and contemporary social theories, it explores how unseen bonds between individuals are shaped through proximity, symbolic interaction, social networks, collective experience, and ethical responsibility. The discussion uses Georg Simmel’s concept of the stranger to explain the paradox of intimacy and distance, while Mead and Cooley’s theories of the social self illuminate how identity is formed through mutual recognition. Goffman’s dramaturgical perspective further frames intimacy as a form of backstage access, where authenticity and vulnerability become central to trust. The essay also engages Granovetter’s distinction between strong and weak ties to show how different forms of social connection contribute to belonging, opportunity, and emotional support. Through Durkheim’s concept of collective effervescence and Buber and Levinas’s ethical philosophies, the paper argues that connection is not only emotional but also moral, requiring care, accountability, and responsibility toward others. Ultimately, the essay positions love and human connection as both sociological realities and poetic mysteries, suggesting that the invisible strings between people are formed, sustained, and transformed through shared meaning, recognition, and the continuous practice of showing up for one another.

In this connection, the research undertaken has been focused on efforts made to negotiate and adopt the final form of the EU-Philippines Framework Agreement on Partnership and Cooperation, a document which provides an enhanced legal framework. In order to achieve this objective, qualitative and quantitative research methods were used. A special attention was also paid to the negotiations for the future EU-Philippines Free Trade Agreement, a legal act which would aid the two parties in achieving mutually beneficial economic goals. To realise this proposed aim, inductive reasoning conducted the research from the specific of the EU-Philippines partnership to the general situations, while deductive reasoning allowed to make an inference by going from general premises to specific conclusions. The research highlighted the Romania-Philippines friendship and the support provided by Romania as an EU Member State in the process of strengthening EU-Philippines relations. To achieve this goal, comparative and analytical methods were used for interpreting information and reach relevant conclusions.

detail.abstract:
This Volume completes the constitutional theory of cryptographic protocols developed in the pre- ceding two Volumes by turning, after architecture (Volume I) and epistemology (Volume II), to historiography and prospect. It identifies three eras of network cooperation, each governed by a distinct value-scaling law and supporting a distinct constitutional form. The Sarnoff era (𝑉 ∝ 𝑁) was the era of broadcast cooperation, in which a sovereign center distributed information and au- thority to a passive periphery; its constitutional achievement was the territorial nation-state and its administrative apparatus. The Metcalfe era (𝑉 ∝ 𝑁2) was the era of bilateral cooperation, in which peer-to-peer connection generated value at quadratic scale; its institutional realization was platform capitalism, in which intermediaries captured the surplus that user-to-user connection produced. The Reed era (𝑉 ∝ 2𝑁 ), now beginning, is the era of group-forming cooperation: com- binatorial subgroup formation generates value at exponential scale and, for the first time in the history of communications networks, is not structurally captured by any intermediary. The cryp- tographic substrate is the first medium that supports Reed-scale value formation without platform extraction.

The Volume develops three substantive theses. First, the three eras are a historical sequence in which each succeeding form does not annihilate the prior form but reorganizes the space of possi- bilities around itself; the Reed era does not abolish Sarnoff and Metcalfe institutions but subsumes them as particular cases of a richer combinatorial topology. Second, the constitutional architecture of the Reed era is three-tiered: a substrate-agnostic cryptographic foundation; tenant-entities (com- panies, decentralized autonomous organizations, voluntary associations) operating on the substrate without owning it; and individuals as final nodes (elos finais) participating in many subgroups si- multaneously across many substrates. Third, the local description of the individual and the global description of the civitas stand in the Bohrian conjugate relation identified in Volume II, but at Reed scale the conjugacy becomes constitutionally structural rather than merely epistemic: the individual cannot be specified independently of the civitas in which his subgroup memberships are constituted, and the civitas cannot be specified independently of the individuals whose memberships constitute it.

The reconstruction of civil society on the cryptographic substrate is unfolding now and will continue through the present century. We are at the beginning of an era whose institutional forms cannot be enumerated in advance. The proper response, reaﬀirmed from Volume II, is Knightian humility paired with the architectural strategy of robust commitment. This Volume specifies the historical and structural conditions under which that humility and that strategy operate.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the arbitrability of antitrust disputes, focusing primarily on India while drawing comparative insights from the United States. It analyses the extent to which competition law claims can be resolved through arbitration, particularly in light of the evolving legal position following Mitsubishi Motors Corp v Soler Chrysler-Plymouth Inc, which recognised the arbitrability of certain antitrust claims in the US. The study also situates this discussion within the broader framework of US antitrust legislation, including the Sherman Act, Clayton Act, Robinson-Patman Act, and the Federal Trade Commission Act.

In the Indian context, the paper focuses on the statutory scheme under the Competition Act 2002, with particular emphasis on s 53N governing compensation claims. It evaluates whether such follow-on claims and other competition disputes can be referred to arbitration, while considering the institutional role of the Competition Commission of India and the limits imposed by public policy.

The paper argues that although arbitration may be suitable for certain private competition claims, core antitrust issues involving market regulation and public interest remain non-arbitrable. It concludes that a balanced and jurisdiction-sensitive approach is necessary to align arbitration with the objectives of competition law without undermining its regulatory framework.

detail.abstract: Οι δημόσιοι υπάλληλοι που βρίσκονται στην πρώτη γραμμή της αλληλεπίδρασης με τους πολίτες, γνωστοί ως «γραφειοκράτες του δρόμου» (Street-Level Bureaucrats - SLBs), αποτελούν την ανθρώπινη όψη του κράτους και τους σιωπηλούς διαμορφωτές της δημόσιας πολιτικής. Το παρόν άρθρο, μέσα από μια εκτενή επισκόπηση της σύγχρονης επιστημονικής βιβλιογραφίας, εξερευνά τη φύση και τη δράση αυτών των κρίσιμων λειτουργών. Εμβαθύνει στο θεωρητικό υπόβαθρο του φαινομένου, με επίκεντρο την έννοια της διακριτικής ευχέρειας [της ελευθερίας δηλαδή που έχουν να λαμβάνουν αποφάσεις] και αναλύει τις στρατηγικές που αναπτύσσουν για να διαχειριστούν τις πιέσεις της καθημερινότητας. Εξετάζονται οι οργανωσιακοί, ατομικοί και κοινωνικοπολιτικοί παράγοντες που πλαισιώνουν τη δράση τους, καθώς και οι σύγχρονες προκλήσεις που αντιμετωπίζουν σε νευραλγικούς τομείς όπως η αγροδασοπονία, η υγεία και η επιβολή του νόμου, ειδικά υπό την επίδραση της ψηφιοποίησης και της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης. Βάσει αυτών, παρουσιάζεται ένα συνθετικό πλαίσιο λύσεων για την ενίσχυση της αποτελεσματικότητας, της ανταπόκρισης και της λογοδοσίας τους, το οποίο περιλαμβάνει την ενδυνάμωση μέσω εκπαίδευσης και πόρων, την προώθηση της προσαρμοστικότητας και την ηθική άσκηση της διακριτικής ευχέρειας. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στο πώς αυτές οι γνώσεις μπορούν να αξιοποιηθούν για την αντιμετώπιση των ιδιαίτερων προκλήσεων της Ελληνικής Δημόσιας Διοίκησης. Τέλος, το άρθρο αναγνωρίζει τους περιορισμούς της παρούσας ανάλυσης και προτείνει κατευθύνσεις για μελλοντική εμπειρική έρευνα, ιδίως στην Ελλάδα.

title:
When Accountability Overreaches:

Proportional Governance and the Misapplication of Financial Investigations in Small Nonprofits

detail.title:
When Accountability Overreaches:

Proportional Governance and the Misapplication of Financial Investigations in Small Nonprofits
detail.abstract:
Small nonprofits operating with volunteer boards and limited financial capacity are increasingly expected to comply with governance and accountability standards developed primarily for larger, professionally resourced organizations. While these expectations aim to strengthen transparency and fiduciary responsibility, they can generate unintended governance effects when applied without regard to organizational scale or capacity.

This paper develops the concept of proportional governance as a framework for aligning oversight mechanisms with the structural realities of small nonprofits. It argues that governance quality is not determined by the intensity or complexity of control systems, but by their fit with organizational size, risk exposure, and operational capacity. Using retrospective financial investigations as a focal point, the paper demonstrates how well-intentioned oversight mechanisms can escalate into open-ended, resource-intensive processes that displace mission activity, weaken board cohesion, and increase organizational vulnerability.

The analysis identifies key governance failure modes in small nonprofits, including informal over-reliance, control escalation, and governance role distortion. It further develops a proportionality-based decision model for financial oversight, emphasizing trigger validity, materiality, scope containment, cost–capacity assessment, and defined closure criteria. In addition, the paper examines the influence of professional expertise on boards, particularly legal framing effects that may unintentionally shift governance toward litigation-oriented reasoning.

At the systems level, the paper argues that mis-scaled governance practices are reinforced by institutional incentives, professional norms, and accountability frameworks designed for larger organizations. It highlights the risk that excessive or unbounded oversight mechanisms may increase, rather than reduce, organizational vulnerability, particularly when they create pathways toward prolonged disputes or litigation with significant financial and operational costs.

The paper concludes that effective governance in small nonprofits requires a recalibration of accountability systems toward proportionality, emphasizing sustainability, contextual judgment, and the containment of oversight processes within defined and feasible boundaries.

title: Does Algorithmic Debiasing Really Improve Fair Lending Compliance?

detail.title: Does Algorithmic Debiasing Really Improve Fair Lending Compliance?
detail.abstract: Algorithmic debiasing ("AD")-a popular machine-learning approach applied to credit scoring models to search for fairer, Less Discriminatory Alternative ("LDA") model versions-is promoted as a means to improve a lender's fair lending performance without sacrificing model predictive accuracy. Using a simple synthetic credit scoring model estimated on publicly available Home Mortgage Disclosure Act ("HMDA") data, I evaluate these claims by performing an in-depth investigation of how such fairness improvements are actually achieved-focusing specifically on the credit profiles of applicants swapped in and out of the debiased model's set of loan approvals. This analysis reveals that-despite claims to the contrary-AD's fairness improvements are not associated with the removal of "artificial, arbitrary, and unnecessary" credit access barriers impeding the approval of otherwise creditworthy individuals. Rather, the AD process simply performs a brute-force reallocation of estimated credit risk away from higher-risk credit profiles correlated with protected class status that were denied by the original model, and toward lowerrisk credit profiles correlated with control group applicants that were Approved by the original model. I argue that this "fairness" improvement is simply surface-level, representing nothing more than the impact of a latent reverse disparate impact encoded into the LDA Model's weights. Apart from the obvious risk and compliance implications of this finding, I also highlight collateral risks to lenders related to UDAAP and ECOA adverse-action compliance. I strongly recommend that lenders adopt mandatory swap-set transparency analyses of this type and share such results with appropriate compliance and risk oversight groups before implementing LDA Models into production.

detail.abstract:
Dimensi “Sosial” dalam rangka kerja Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) semakin mendapat perhatian sebagai penentu utama kelestarian organisasi, khususnya dalam landskap pasca-pandemik yang menyaksikan perubahan mendalam terhadap struktur pekerjaan, pola kerja fleksibel, dan kesejahteraan psikososial pekerja. Artikel ulasan naratif ini bertujuan mensintesis secara kritis literatur berkaitan keseimbangan kerja-kehidupan dan kesihatan mental pekerja dalam konteks ESG melalui aplikasi Model Tuntutan–Sumber Pekerjaan (Job Demands-Resources Model, JD-R), dengan tumpuan khusus kepada implikasi terhadap tenaga kerja di Sabah, Malaysia. Menggunakan pendekatan sintesis naratif berasaskan ENTREQ, artikel ini meneliti literatur daripada pangkalan data Scopus, Web of Science, dan Google Scholar bagi tempoh 2015–2026. Analisis tematik refleksif mengenal pasti empat tema utama: (1) evolusi konseptual dimensi sosial ESG dalam pengurusan sumber manusia strategik; (2) hubungan antara tuntutan pekerjaan digital, kerja hibrid, dan kesejahteraan psikologi pekerja; (3) kapasiti institusi dan pemegang taruh dalam melaksanakan agenda kesejahteraan pekerja; serta (4) kerangka dasar dan perundangan yang membentuk perlindungan kesejahteraan psikososial pekerja. Dapatan menunjukkan bahawa integrasi ESG tanpa kerangka psikososial berasaskan teori seperti JD-R cenderung menghasilkan pelaksanaan simbolik dan tidak substantif. Dalam konteks Sabah, kekangan struktur ekonomi, ketidakseimbangan sektor formal-informal, serta keterbatasan infrastruktur kesihatan mental memperkukuh kerentanan pekerja terhadap tekanan pekerjaan pasca-pandemik. Artikel ini menyumbang kepada pengembangan teori hubungan pekerjaan dengan mencadangkan kerangka analitikal integratif ESG–JD-R sebagai asas kepada pembentukan polisi buruh, strategi organisasi, dan reformasi institusi buruh yang lebih responsif.

title: Revocable Delegation: Selective Overruling under Double-Sided Information Asymmetry
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University (NTU) - Division of Economics and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Revocable Delegation: Selective Overruling under Double-Sided Information Asymmetry
detail.abstract: We develop a theory of revocable delegation in organizations. Building on Aghion and Tirole (1997), we argue that an informed principal should not always overrule an agent's recommendation, even when intervention raises current payoff. Overruling has two opposing effects: it discourages initiative by reducing the agent's expected implementation authority, but it also disciplines corner-cutting by making discretion revocable. We incorporate loss aversion to show that being overruled is experienced as a psychologically salient loss, which sharpens both effects. The principal therefore optimally chooses selective rather than systematic intervention. The model links authority, incomplete contracts, and behavioral economics, and offers a unified account of why effective organizations often rely on controlled opacity rather than full transparency or unconditional delegation.

title: The Entropic Theory of the Firm: Operational Entropy, Managerial Blindness, and the Thermodynamics of Corporate Survival

detail.title: The Entropic Theory of the Firm: Operational Entropy, Managerial Blindness, and the Thermodynamics of Corporate Survival
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a thermodynamic model of corporate fragility linking managerial blindness (forecasting error), structural complexity (assets/gross profit), and operational dissipation (opex/revenue). Operational entropy S = (E·φ) + δ(1+φ)^k grows exponentially with complexity. The entropic yield H = (R−S)/S partitions firms into stable, fragile, and collapsing regimes. The model requires only public 10-K data and guidance. Case studies: NVIDIA, Volkswagen, Lehman.

It shows that GSTS devolution created new pathways to provincial revenue mobilisation, although it did not necessarily predetermine the tax performance. In Balochistan, GSTS potential is concentrated to limited sectors, however actual GSTS collection is less due to inaccurate forecasting, poor harmonisation and administrative constraint. The research paper examines that the decentralised GSTS is most successful when a legal assignment aligns with sector onboarding, viable compliance mechanisms, improved digital administration, realistic forecasting, and cooperation between different jurisdictions.

title: The Citizens Standard: A Framework for a Citizens-First Monetary Reform

detail.title: The Citizens Standard: A Framework for a Citizens-First Monetary Reform

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a constitutional monetary framework governed by three variables working in coordination: population determines when new money is created, GDP calibrates how much, and a permanently frozen circulating money supply ensures the active economy is never diluted. The circulating money supply is frozen at its current level — no new money enters the spending economy under any circumstances. New retirement money is created through two mechanisms: K1, triggered by each new verified citizen through birth or naturalization; and K2, triggered by real economic growth and distributed to all existing citizens. Both streams are deposited into locked, individually owned retirement accounts invested in the total United States stock market index by default. Inflation from retirement issuance is deferred, bounded, predictable, and occurs only at retirement age when accounts unlock in known, scheduled waves.

title: Informal Transport Integration and Resilience: Evidence from the Taxi Sector in Yaounde, Cameroon

detail.title: Informal Transport Integration and Resilience: Evidence from the Taxi Sector in Yaounde, Cameroon

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the European Union through the MoVe Urban Mobility Project. The views expressed in this paper are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of the funding organization.

detail.abstract:
Informal transport systems are a cornerstone of urban mobility in Sub-Saharan African cities, yet their economic magnitude, operational dynamics, and integration potential remain poorly documented in the empirical literature. This paper examines the taxi sector in Yaoundé, Cameroon, drawing on three original datasets collected under the EU-funded MoVe Urban Mobility Project, including an exhaustive census of 17,726 active taxis.

We introduce the Informal Transport Integration and Resilience Index (ITIRI), a novel composite indicator designed to measure operator performance across four dimensions: economic viability, urban integration, social accessibility, and operational resilience. Scores are constructed through min-max normalization and equal-weight aggregation across 20 variables. Econometric analysis (OLS regression) identifies the key determinants of integration capacity, while K-means clustering reveals three structurally distinct operator profiles within the sector.

Our findings demonstrate that the taxi sector constitutes a major pillar of Yaoundé's urban economy, generating an estimated 80 billion FCFA in annual revenues and supporting up to 100,000 direct and indirect jobs based on the census sample, figures that may reach 180 billion FCFA and 1.2 million daily passengers when extrapolated to the full estimated fleet of 40,000 vehicles. Despite this economic weight, ITIRI scores remain uniformly low (no operator reaches the 'high integration' threshold), driven primarily by fleet aging, high operating costs, and distance intensity. These results provide robust empirical grounds for inclusive urban transport reform policies targeting informal operator formalization and BRT corridor integration in African cities.

title: Converging on Disclosure

detail.title: Converging on Disclosure

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute - Law Working Paper No. 923/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI) - Law Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
In Disclosureland, Atinuke Adediran offers a powerful and timely account of how corporate racial disclosures function not just as mere statements of corporate virtue, but as instruments of governance. The book demonstrates that racial progress in corporate America has historically depended on federal intervention—particularly through disclosure mandates, contracting requirements, and civil rights enforcement—and that voluntary corporate commitments, absent regulatory backbone, are fragile and prone to retrenchment. In doing so, Disclosureland makes an invaluable contribution to the literature by revealing disclosure as a structural mechanism through which the federal government has shaped the governance of issues related to race within corporate firms. Yet the book implicitly assumes that meaningful federal disclosure reform depends upon political consensus around demographic diversity as a shared social good. In today’s polarized environment—marked by backlash against DEI initiatives, litigation invoking Reconstruction-era statutes, and contested narratives about racial equity—that consensus appears elusive. If diversity itself is politically divisive, the path to mandatory corporate racial disclosure seems blocked.

This Essay argues that disclosure may nevertheless be politically and normatively viable—not because Americans agree about diversity, but because ideological opponents may converge on transparency itself. Drawing on Derrick Bell’s interest-convergence thesis and contemporary elaborations, this Essay contends that both advocates and critics of corporate racial justice initiatives have incentives to demand data: Progressives require information to measure stagnation and enforce accountability, while conservative critics require demographic transparency to assess claims of overreach or unlawful favoritism. The primary resistance to disclosure lies not in ideological disagreement, but in corporate preference for opacity. By reframing racial disclosure as a civic obligation of corporate personhood—grounded in transparency rather than moral consensus—this Essay extends Disclosureland’s insights and identifies a politically feasible route toward federal disclosure mandates. In an era saturated with corporate speech, the most transformative intervention may be insisting not on agreement, but on measurable truth.

title: Government as GP or LP? Public Limited Partner Capital Reallocates Deals within VC Firms — Evidence from Japan's JIC

detail.title: Government as GP or LP? Public Limited Partner Capital Reallocates Deals within VC Firms — Evidence from Japan's JIC

detail.abstract:
How does government limited partner (LP) capital affect venture capital outcomes? Using Japan Investment Corporation (JIC) — a setting that allows direct observation of within–general partner (GP) variation in LP composition — this study analyzes a deal-by-fund panel of 2,976 observations covering 21 JIC-backed GPs and a mechanically constructed control of 16 independent GPs from the PitchBook Japan VC top-32 ranking.

Government LP capital operates through allocation rather than transformation. GP-level effects are statistically indistinguishable from zero (baseline 95% CI = [−8.0, +10.0]pp), while within-GP variation shows that deals funded through JIC-backed funds are 7.3 percentage points more likely to receive follow-on financing within 24 months (p = 0.017). When both margins are estimated jointly, the within-GP effect remains significant and the GP-level effect is absorbed to zero.

The allocation effect is heterogeneous in firms' prior funding history: +15.0pp at initial-round firms with no prior funding (p = 0.045) and −14.5pp at three prior rounds (p = 0.025; interaction p = 0.0015). The pattern is consistent with certification under information uncertainty, although this study does not directly identify the underlying mechanism.

Results are robust to alternative horizons (12/24/36 months), staggered difference-in-differences estimators, event-study diagnostics (pre-trend p = 0.258), placebo tests, and a pre-treatment universe reconstruction with entropy balancing (+7.22pp). Government LP capital does not detectably transform receiving GPs; its observable effect appears through fund-level allocation within GPs, and is concentrated among firms with little prior funding history. The policy implication is to target the segments where this allocation channel concentrates rather than to focus on selecting high-performing GPs.

title: Institutional Prerequisites for Defence Conversion: A Comparative Industrial Policy Framework for Ontario's Automotive Sector

detail.title: Institutional Prerequisites for Defence Conversion: A Comparative Industrial Policy Framework for Ontario's Automotive Sector
detail.abstract: Ontario's automotive sector faces simultaneous structural shocks from trade policy uncertainty, the EV transition, and shrinking U.S. market access. Defence procurement has emerged as one potential retooling pathway following Canada's first Defence Industrial Strategy (2026) and the Regional Defence Investment Initiative. This paper argues that defence conversion is primarily an institutional design problem rather than a technical one. Drawing on a most-different systems comparison of Ukraine (Brave1), Germany (VW/IG Metall), and Japan/South Korea (Chaebol/Keiretsu), it develops an eight-factor Conditional Policy Architecture and Conversion Readiness Scorecard. Assessed based on the case studies and validated through a Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis, the paper places Ontario at 1.15/3.0 ("emerging but not yet viable"), identifying three binding Tier-1 constraints: intermediary institutions, certification pathways, and labour co-governance. Finally, a Transferability Matrix evaluates which design principles travel to Ontario's liberal-market context, offering policymakers a diagnostic tool for targeted institutional reform.

detail.abstract: This research examines the historical and contemporary discriminatory of communities formerly stigmatised as “untouchable” and historically constituted through heterogeneous identities (Ati-Shudras, Out-castes,Depressed Class, Mahar, Dalit), later consolidated as Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) under the Constitution of India 1950. It argued caste as a durable political economy of graded inequality, structured by ritualised hierarchies, occupational immobility, and asymmetric access to land, education, and state power. This research analysis against Brahminical and Orthodox normative–legal traditions (Manusmriti, YajnavalkyaSmriti, and Narada Smriti within the Dharmashastra corpus) argued anti-caste emancipatory interventions by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, tracing how constitutional safeguards and policies transformed these fragmented social groups into administratively and politically “homogeneous” categories for the purposes of equal representation and welfare. Empirical data analysis and social stratification frameworks, along with historical institutionalism, declined traditional businesses groups and communities, privatisation and jurisprudential interpretation, the research assesses the August 2024 deliberations of the Supreme Court of India on SC/ST “sub-classification” and the extension of the “creamy layer” (income cap), evaluating their long-term adverse effects and constitutional implications. It argues that these interventions risk weakening substantive equality and creating bottlenecks in future economic growth by reinforcing structural distortions within India’s federal and constitutional framework.

title: AURORA: A Distributed Passive Cognitive Architecture for Airspace Awareness in Contested Environments

detail.title: AURORA: A Distributed Passive Cognitive Architecture for Airspace Awareness in Contested Environments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no financial support for the research, authorship, and/or publication of this article.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces AURORA, a distributed passive cognitive architecture designed to enhance airspace awareness in contested electromagnetic environments. Traditional active radar systems, while effective in long-range detection, inherently expose themselves through electromagnetic emissions, rendering them vulnerable to electronic intelligence (ELINT) exploitation and anti-radiation threats. In contrast, purely passive sensing approaches, despite their low observability, often suffer from high uncertainty and limited target confirmation capability.

AURORA addresses this fundamental trade-off by proposing a hybrid, network-centric paradigm that integrates passive multi-domain sensing, cognitive processing, and airborne provocation mechanisms within a unified architectural framework. At its core, the system relies on a distributed network of ground-based passive nodes—conceptualized in this study as a “Defensive Farm” architecture—which operate as spatially dispersed sensing units capable of continuously monitoring the environment without emitting detectable signals. These nodes are complemented by lightweight airborne platforms, termed Micro-AWACS (Micro Airborne Warning and Control Systems), which function not only as controlled active sensors but also as cognitive agents capable of inducing adversarial reactions to reveal otherwise concealed information.

The proposed architecture is structured into four interdependent layers: distributed sensing, resilient communication, cognitive processing, and command-and-control (C2). Through multi-sensor data fusion and probabilistic inference, AURORA transforms fragmented and uncertain observations into coherent situational awareness. A key innovation lies in the introduction of cognitive provocation, wherein detection is no longer limited to passive observation but is actively enhanced by shaping the adversary’s behavior.

Furthermore, the paper presents an integrated conceptual model in which situational awareness emerges as a dynamic function of sensing, provocation, networking, and survivability. The system operates as an adaptive feedback loop, continuously refining its internal state based on environmental interaction. This approach effectively shifts the paradigm from platform-centric sensing to network-centric cognition, and from static observation to interactive perception.

The findings suggest that AURORA provides a robust and scalable framework for next-generation air defense and surveillance systems, particularly in environments characterized by electronic warfare, signal denial, and high operational uncertainty. By leveraging the synergy between passive sensing and controlled active intervention, the architecture significantly enhances both survivability and detection reliability, offering a viable pathway toward resilient and intelligent situational awareness systems.
